follow-up time: From 24 weeks gestation to postpartum period
cohort: 2972 pregnant women at Bahrain Defence Force Hospital, West Riffa, Bahrain, from September 2019 to August 2020
finding: Higher BMI during pregnancy was associated with increased risks of hypertension, antepartum hemorrhage, postpartum complications, and longer hospital stay, but not with increased risks of gestational diabetes, induction of labor, or cesarean birth.
mod_finding: Maternal obesity was not associated with an increased risk of cesarean birth.
